title: Verifier-Guided Repair Improves Validator-Checked Vendor-CLI Configurations: A Preregistered Paired Fault-Injection Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution declared the model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, expand experimental-design rationale, interpret discordant-pair structure via representative validator traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A commonly advocated safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): generate a candidate configuration, check it with a deterministic verifier, and when violations are found feed precise diagnostics back to a generator/repair model for correction. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs. Field and survey studies caution that read-oriented LLM assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes.

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. Verifier-guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates activate the verifier; to ensure activation in a paired, controlled comparison we used deterministically injected controlled faults that are reused across conditions. Our preregistered research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair pipelines have been studied across code, IaC, and DSL domains. Controlled evaluations and benchmarks show that deterministic verifiers interposed between generation and acceptance raise verifier-detected pass rates and that providing verifier diagnostics to a repair model increases the chance that a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [1,2]. Complementary studies document caveats: (i) single-proxy verifiers can be optimized around by models (verifier-exploitation) producing pathological refinements [3]; (ii) verifier-mediated loops impose measurable interaction/compute overheads (the "verifier tax") whose magnitude depends on horizon and design choices [4]; and (iii) field work in NetOps highlights the gap between helpful read-oriented assistance and safe autonomous remediation in production operator streams [5].

Synthesis and gap. The supplied empirical literature establishes that verifier-guided repair improves verifier pass rates in code/IaC benchmarks but leaves open how those gains translate to vendor CLI templates under deterministic, preregistered controlled faults and under paired shared-candidate semantics. Our study addresses this gap by (a) forcing verifier activation with deterministic fault injection, (b) using a paired design that reuses the same injected candidate across arms (thereby isolating diagnostics exposure), and (c) preregistering both the primary estimand and safety aggregation rules so that confirmatory results are auditable against a frozen plan.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where per-pair success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check to agree on acceptance.

Adapter and pairing semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each task index a single deterministic controlled-fault candidate was injected and that same candidate was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Under this contract baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Because the two arms share the same initial candidate and matched repair budgets, observed differences isolate diagnostics exposure rather than differences in source generation or fault assignment.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. Confirmatory execution declared the model gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter contract produced exactly one sampled initial generation per task that was reused by both arms; the design therefore does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge fault bank and scoring. We preregistered 40 deterministic controlled-fault task indices (task indices 1..40) produced by a deterministic fault injector applied to synthetic vendor-CLI templates. The primary success predicate required agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. A harmful-change labeling mapping (frozen before execution) classifies post-repair validation traces containing PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE as harmful; that mapping and all per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution to permit deterministic independent reaggregation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic.

Statistical analysis plan. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We prespecified reporting of discordant counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness handling followed the preregistered rule 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); sensitivity analyses treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations were recorded during execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed_pairs = 39 (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered complete-pair rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507. Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excluded one pair because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were recorded in the execution manifest.

Representative failure-mode diagnostics. Per-episode validator traces and repair transcripts recorded during execution illustrate mechanisms behind the aggregate contrast. Representative examples from the archived traces:
- task-000003 (hard, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change pattern): baseline repair produced post-repair validation containing PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE, and FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH and received score = 0; the guarded repair avoided the protected-interface change and received score = 1. This episode is one of the observed guarded-only successes and documents a common pattern where exposed violation codes explicitly identified the offending protected field (PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE) and the guarded repair omitted that change.
- task-000002 (hard, make_before_break_uplink_switchover pattern): both baseline and guarded returned the same correct repair in this case (n11), showing that when the initial post-fault source already encoded the required safe sequence the repair step is redundant.
- task-000001 (medium, shutdown_configure_restore pattern): both conditions produced accepted repairs but in different edit orders; guarded episodes often contain explicit validator_trace.violation_codes exposed to the model that appear to guide command ordering.

These representative traces show that (a) diagnostics sometimes direct repairs away from protected-interface edits or toward restoring required command sequences, and (b) not all tasks required diagnostic assistance because some source candidates were already correct. The per-episode traces and the frozen harmful-change mapping permit deterministic re-computation of per-episode harmful-change tallies; because the archived confirmatory summary did not include the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation it remains unresolved for confirmatory inference here.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the primary contrast. The paired design isolates the effect of exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics: both arms received the same deterministic controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets, so the observed increase (≈20.51 percentage points) is attributable to diagnostics exposure under the adapter contract. The discordant-pair breakdown (n10 = 9 vs n01 = 1) shows that when repairs differ they predominantly favor the guarded condition; exact paired testing yields p = 0.02148 supporting that this imbalance is unlikely under a null of no paired difference at the prespecified alpha.

Mechanism and failure-mode patterning. Analysis of archived validator traces and representative task manifests indicates two recurring mechanisms by which diagnostics improved outcomes: (1) explicit identification of protected fields (violation code PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE) prevented repairs that would change guarded interfaces, and (2) violation codes describing missing required-command sequences (e.g., FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH after a shutdown–change step) prompted repairs that reintroduced omitted restore steps. Representative task difficulty metadata in the archived task manifest show medium- and hard-pattern examples where diagnostics changed repair outcomes; these per-episode examples are consistent with the aggregate discordant structure but do not imply uniform benefits across all fault classes.

Statistical uncertainty, power, and ceiling effects. With complete_pairs = 39 the observed paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the absolute difference excludes zero and ranges from approximately 7.69 to 35.90 percentage points, indicating a materially positive effect but appreciable remaining uncertainty about the upper bound. The preregistered power calculus targeted larger planning effect sizes (~30 percentage points) for n=40; the observed effect (~20.5 points) was detectable given the observed discordant counts but would have required larger sample sizes for narrower CIs or precise per-fault-class inference. The observed marginal success rates (baseline 76.9%, guarded 97.4%) also indicate a nontrivial ceiling: many tasks are repairable even without diagnostics, and diagnostic exposure primarily benefits a subset of fault patterns that produce actionable validator feedback.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved verifier+simulator-validated success on this controlled bank, but verifier-guided workflows impose extra model–verifier interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the declared maximum of 120. These counts allow exploratory calculation of cost per avoided failure, but assessing operational feasibility (the verifier tax tradeoffs) requires broader deployment-scale studies beyond this controlled experiment.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the analysis executor; because that aggregation was not computed there is no confirmatory safety verdict in this paper. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution contain the exact inputs required for deterministic recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary should be treated as exploratory.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing and exactly-one sampled initial generation per pair ensure isolation of diagnostics exposure but preclude measuring effects of independent first-pass sampling; the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset), which is not evidence of deterministic sampling. Construct validity: primary success requires agreement between a deterministic verifier and a simulator; both components constrain what “valid” operationally means. External validity: the testbed used synthetic, template-based vendor-CLI faults and a single declared model (gpt-5-mini); generalization to diverse vendor devices and live operator streams is limited. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 suffices to detect the observed aggregate contrast but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class claims. Verifier-exploitation remains a theoretical concern for longer-horizon agentic pipelines; our short-horizon single-repair budget and paired design mitigate some exploitation modes but do not eliminate multi-step pathologies.

Recommended next steps. Deterministic recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (using the recorded mapping and validation traces) is a necessary follow-up for a confirmatory safety verdict. Complementary replications should (a) broaden task distributions toward field-sourced incidents, (b) evaluate multiple models and verifier ensembles, and (c) instrument end-to-end cost/latency tradeoffs at production scale to bound the verifier tax under realistic routing of requests.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter with shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This result is valid under the adapter's shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic validator and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction. We recommend deterministic recomputation of the preregistered safety aggregation, multi-model and multi-verifier replications, and larger-scale operational cost/latency studies to evaluate deployment feasibility and multi-step safety in agentic NetOps pipelines.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
